meta.how_html:
• Budget. Each country and channel spends its 2026 budget again in 2027: observed spend through 2026-10-05 plus the media plan after it, over the 2026 planning year (2025-12-29 to 2026-12-21). The 2027 spend is flat, the same amount every ISO week of 2027 (52 weeks). Week 53 of 2026 (Monday 2026-12-28, which holds Jan 1–3 2027) is spent at the 2027 rate and counted in neither budget. Its cohort counts with 2026.
  • Total paid DAU = 2027 cohorts + 2026 cohorts (both modelled) + the pre-2026 base (observed, then extended). Past weeks use observed new profiles and activations, and the curves only going forward: the published-forecast basis. The three component lines are medians, so they do not add exactly to the total's median.
  • Scope. All paid cohorts is total paid DAU. Acquired in the same year counts only cohorts acquired in the week's own ISO year: 2026 weeks count 2026 cohorts (week 53 included) and 2027 weeks count 2027 cohorts, so 2027 starts from zero and the pre-2026 base never counts. The scope applies to DAU and MAU.
  • MAU = global paid DAU × 4.792, a fixed ratio rather than a modelled one, estimated from global paid media (analysis). Everything on this page is global for that reason. Daily MAU = the week's MAU × a day-of-week factor (Mon 0.9871 … Sun 1.0129), so a week's days average back to its weekly value.
  • Scenarios. Flat budget: each country × channel spends its 2026 budget again, flat. Optimized for Dec-15 MAU: the same 2027 total, still flat weekly within each country × channel, reallocated by GMIO's optimizer to maximize MAU on Dec 15, 2027, with each cell between −100% and +500% of its 2026 budget. The optimizer maximizes the p10 (90%-confident) level on the incremental basis, and every figure shown is then re-projected on the attributed basis. Flat weekly spend means the two weeks after Dec 15 are spent although they cannot move MAU on Dec 15. 0 of 58 cells end at +500% and 6 at −100%, so the bounds, not only the curves, shape the result.
  • Dec-15 MAU is MAU on the day of Dec 15, 2027 (a Wednesday): the week of 12/13's MAU × 0.9957. It is not a 4-week average.
  • Dec-15 DAU is the mean over ISO weeks 47–50 of each year (2026: 11/16–12/7; 2027: 11/22–12/13).
  • Bands are the central 90% interval over 1000 draws. Total is summed within each draw, so channel intervals do not add. They cover the curves' parameter uncertainty only, not the MAU ratio and not the plan.
meta.caveats_html:
• Hypothetical. Flat budget, flat weekly spend, every 2026 market kept. No seasonality, no creative or bidding changes after the latest refresh, and no cross-channel interaction, so combined figures are an upper bound.
  • The 2027 tail is extrapolated. 2026 cohorts reach ~100 weeks since install by late 2027, while the retention curves are fitted on up to about 70 weeks (UAC) and 48 (Meta Android). Retention is evaluated to 156 weeks here, against 52 in production.
  • Curves 2026-10-12 (fitted through 2026-10-05) carry convergence warnings on UAC CPI and Meta Android activations, and their interval calibration is unverified. Treat the bands as indicative.
  • MAU is a multiplier, not a model. 4.792 × paid DAU (how it was estimated) is a global ratio. It assumes the MAU/DAU ratio holds as the cohort mix shifts toward newer cohorts in 2027, and it is applied unchanged to UAC and Meta Android separately.
